Open the trainer

Tap Ask trainer on Today. To build a plan, open Plan > New block or New workout and choose the trainer. You can also open the trainer during a session.

The trainer needs Block Pro and iOS 27. An eligible new account may be offered days of Pro. Settings > AI > AI trainer shows your access and messages left.

It can read your training log, build workouts and blocks, change unlogged sets, and explain your results. It cannot cancel a subscription or delete your account.

Build a program

  1. Open Plan > New block > Build with trainer. Answer the questions about your goal, week and equipment. Saved answers are prefilled.
  2. Review your answers and first day, then tap Build draft. To discuss an idea first, choose Talk it through on New block.
  3. Tap Review program. Check the workouts, sets, training days, and weeks. Edit anything you want to change before you tap Apply program.

“Build a six-week strength program. Four days a week, 60 minutes per session. Add core work.”

A program can use 1 to 16 weeks, with a deload when the program calls for one. For a rolling cycle, the trainer writes the workouts to fit that schedule.

Review next targets

After you save a session, the trainer can propose each lift's next load and reps. It reads the loads, reps, effort, notes, rep ranges, and week of the training block. The result appears on the finish page, in the chat, and on Today while it waits for review.

Each changed lift shows its current sets, proposed sets, and a reason. Approve saves that line to the workout. Reject leaves it unchanged. Approve all and Reject all decide the remaining lines. A hold needs no decision.

The app never changes a load by itself. Until you approve a new target, the next session starts at the numbers you lifted with Pro, or at the workout's numbers without it.

Read lamps and next targets for the details, including deloads and set feedback.

Change a session or workout

Between sets, ask for a swap, a lighter session, or a lift added or removed. Say whether it is for today only or the workout too. The trainer does not change a lift after you have logged a set for it in the open session.

“The rack is taken. Replace back squats with a machine lift for today.”

A change to a saved workout opens with Review workout. The review lists the old and new sets. Check it, then apply it. Saving a workout change does not start a session. If the proposal also changes today's session, the review includes both parts.

For a one-session change, check the proposal before applying it. Dismiss leaves your plan as it is.

Your notes and rules

About you holds your goal, equipment, schedule, and lifts to avoid. Your rules file holds preferences you want the trainer to use again. A lift's note is the place for a specific request, such as a warm-up pattern or a load to try next time.

Ask the trainer to add or change a rule. Review the proposal before saving it. A note about pain or fatigue also helps it explain why a lift should hold.

The trainer uses research cards with sources and can search the web when needed. Its citations explain the evidence behind a suggestion. They do not guarantee a result. It gives no medical advice; for pain or an injury, stop that movement and seek appropriate care.

Models and allowance

Claude answers through Block after you allow it. Pro includes up to 120 Claude messages per month, within $3.00 of included AI usage. No extra charge is made when the limit is reached. A long program build uses more of that allowance. The count resets on the first of the month; tool steps within a message do not count as extra messages.

Training numbers and programs use Claude Sonnet 5. App help, feedback, and other questions use Haiku 4.5. The line under the chat field names the model and shows what is left. Tap it to open About the trainer.

You can use your own Claude key. It uses Sonnet 5 for every message, with separate billing from Anthropic and no monthly limit from Block. Block Pro is still required.

Where your data goes

Through Block, your question and the training data needed to answer it go to Anthropic through Block's server. Your name and email are left out. Block counts usage but does not store the questions and answers on its server. The chat is stored on your iPhone.

With your own key, requests go directly from your iPhone to Anthropic. Your key stays in that iPhone's Keychain. Read the privacy policy for details.

When an answer does not arrive

  • Not answered: use Try again, or edit the question and send it again.
  • Message or AI usage limit reached: check the reset date or use your own Claude key. Your existing chat remains readable.
  • Pro access changed: check Settings > Block Pro. If you just bought Pro, restore the purchase to the correct account.
  • Needs iOS 27: the built-in trainer cannot answer on an earlier version. Connected assistants use their own apps.

A failed answer does not apply a proposal. If a problem continues, contact support with the message you see.
